\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{شہنشاہ} (shahanshāh)}{شہنشاہ (shahanshāh)}]{\ur{شہنشاہ} (shahanshāh) — an emperor}

\label{lesson:UR-C308-shahanshah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a slap, then the Urdu for to twist.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{شہنشاہ}}
\textbf{\ur{شہنشاہ}} — \emph{shahanshāh} — \textquotedblleft{}an emperor\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{شہنشاہ} \ur{ایک} \ur{بڑے} \ur{محل} \ur{میں} \ur{رہتا} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shahanshāh ek baṛe mahal meṅ rahtā thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The emperor lived in a great palace.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{شہنشاہ}} (\emph{shahanshāh}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{shāhanshāh}, \textquotedblleft{}king of kings\textquotedblright{}, built from \emph{shāh}, a king, the word inside \textbf{\ur{بادشاہ}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shahanshāh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shahanshāh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shahanshāh ek baṛe mahal meṅ rahtā thā.} — The emperor lived in a great palace.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a slap, then the Urdu for to twist, then say \emph{shahanshāh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{شہنشاہ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An emperor\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تخت} (takht)}{تخت (takht)}]{\ur{تخت} (takht) — a throne}

\label{lesson:UR-C308-takht}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to twist, then the Urdu for an emperor.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تخت}}
\textbf{\ur{تخت}} — \emph{takht} — \textquotedblleft{}a throne\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بادشاہ} \ur{تخت} \ur{پر} \ur{بیٹھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bādshāh takht par baiṭhā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The king sat on the throne.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تخت}} (\emph{takht}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{takht}, \textquotedblleft{}a throne, a raised wooden seat\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ur{تخت} \ur{پر} \ur{بیٹھنا}} is to come to the throne.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{takht}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{takht}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bādshāh takht par baiṭhā.} — The king sat on the throne.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to twist, then the Urdu for an emperor, then say \emph{takht} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{تخت} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A throne\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تاج} (tāj)}{تاج (tāj)}]{\ur{تاج} (tāj) — a crown}

\label{lesson:UR-C308-taj}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an emperor, then the Urdu for a throne.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تاج}}
\textbf{\ur{تاج}} — \emph{tāj} — \textquotedblleft{}a crown\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{تاج} \ur{پہنا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{us ne tāj pahnā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He put on the crown.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تاج}} (\emph{tāj}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{tāj}, \textquotedblleft{}a crown\textquotedblright{}. It is masculine: \textbf{\ur{تاج} \ur{پہنا}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for an emperor, then the Urdu for a throne, then say \emph{tāj} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دربار} (darbār)}{دربار (darbār)}]{\ur{دربار} (darbār) — a royal court}

\label{lesson:UR-C308-darbar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a throne, then the Urdu for a crown.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دربار}}
\textbf{\ur{دربار}} — \emph{darbār} — \textquotedblleft{}a royal court\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دربار} \ur{میں} \ur{سب} \ur{خاموش} \ur{تھے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{darbār meṅ sab khāmosh the.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Everyone at court was silent.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{دربار}} (\emph{darbār}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{darbār}, \textquotedblleft{}a royal court\textquotedblright{}: the hall where the king sat and heard his people.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{darbār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{darbār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{darbār meṅ sab khāmosh the.} — Everyone at court was silent.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a throne, then the Urdu for a crown, then say \emph{darbār} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{وارث} (vāris)}{وارث (vāris)}]{\ur{وارث} (vāris) — an heir}

\label{lesson:UR-C308-varis}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a crown, then the Urdu for a royal court.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{وارث}}
\textbf{\ur{وارث}} — \emph{vāris} — \textquotedblleft{}an heir\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بادشاہ} \ur{کا} \ur{کوئی} \ur{وارث} \ur{نہیں} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bādshāh kā koī vāris nahīṅ thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The king had no heir.
\end{quote}

Masculine or feminine, by the person meant.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{وارث}} (\emph{vāris}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{wārith}, \textquotedblleft{}one who inherits\textquotedblright{}. Urdu says its last letter as \emph{s}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vāris}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vāris}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bādshāh kā koī vāris nahīṅ thā.} — The king had no heir.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a crown, then the Urdu for a royal court, then say \emph{vāris} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{وارث} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An heir\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
